Hi Elena — great to hear from you and thanks for outlining the ask. High level options we typically use: 

1) One‑time evidence delivery fee (SOW/exhibit)
   - Fixed price to cover engineering time to produce artifacts, run verification tests, and deliver the acceptance packet.
   - Good when customer wants a discrete deliverable that can be acceptance‑gated before production flip.

2) Annual compliance credit blended into committed pricing
   - We amortize the effort across the annual contract as a recurring credit (e.g., $X/year for the duration of the term).
   - Better for procurement forecasting but requires a short acceptance checklist to close the credit milestone.

3) Hybrid (recommended for pilots)
   - Small one‑time SOW for initial evidence + a modest annual credit for ongoing audit support and retention (covers future evidence snapshots and limited re‑attestations).

What the evidence package includes (standard):
- Audit log export sample + retention policy doc (configurable retention tiers)
- KMS/HSM integration checklist and key custody notes (HSM attestation summary if requested)
- SRE runbook for evidence reproduction (replay steps, tooling)
- Acceptance checklist and delivery SOW (signature milestone)

I've attached a short SOW template and cost worksheet. If Procurement prefers the annual credit route, we can show the blended economics side‑by‑side.

Recommendation for MediCenter: hybrid approach for the pilot — one‑time SOW of ~€12k for evidence packaging and integration verification, plus a €6k/year compliance credit if you sign a 12‑month committed tier. This keeps procurement happy with predictable TCO while giving security a discrete acceptance gate.

If that looks reasonable I can draft the exhibit and loop in Finance (Ben Carter) to finalize payment terms.

- €12k one‑time SOW: book as implementation revenue (recognize on delivery/acceptance).
